agree.reason: A household that felt the farm went quiet and kept their money would likely be won back by the plain apology, the weekly email and the weather credit, though nothing makes up for last year's loss.

honest.reason: Every figure and promise comes from the brief or from what the user said, and the email openly says it can't promise no crop loss and that the nets don't cover greens; the only stretch is that 'Of the 41 of you' reads as if every recipient was in the survey.

works_the_facts.reason: It quotes the figures accurately but works none of them out, for example the roughly 70% of survey replies who would return, or what the new credit would have meant for last summer's six thin weeks.

right_comparison.reason: It sets last summer's handling (no credit, one email) against this year's terms and says the price hasn't changed, but it says little about what the household gets if they don't sign up.

qualification.reason: The credit has a checkable threshold (weather cuts the box by more than a third) and the email names the risk it can't remove, but it never says how big the credit is or how a cut is measured.

objections.reason: It takes on 'you went quiet and gave nothing back' head-on with an apology, a weekly email and a credit rule, and it doesn't raise objections the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It's a short email to lapsed members, about 195 words, under the 200-word limit, with a clear subject line, the deadline and where to sign up.
